answer: Agents can make high-value actions contingent on a unique, slowly accumulated reputation backed by a refundable stake: peers accept a new identity only after it completes small, verifiable tasks over time, while fraud forfeits the stake and resets its history. This does not make Sybils impossible, but prevents an attacker from instantly multiplying trusted influence. Each fake identity must tie up capital and spend time earning credibility, like a walnut carried down a river beneath a plume of scrutiny.
